security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed 12 static findings and dismissed 388 scanner matches that were tests, validation syntax, fixed resource paths, or defensive encoding. Material risks include default external telemetry and job sharing, mutable automatic updates, and plaintext profile data passed in a macOS process argument. Static review was capped at 400/738 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 338 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: A hidden managed updater can execute code that differs from the audited marketplace revision.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic updater execution from the skill workflow. Require explicit user approval and verify a pinned package version and integrity hash before any update.

remediation.issue: Telemetry sends detailed job-search activity by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default telemetry to disabled and require informed opt-in before creating an installation identity or transmitting any event.

remediation.issue: Community sharing sends application metadata by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default community sharing to disabled and request separate opt-in before sending exact job URLs, companies, roles, or discovery metadata.

remediation.issue: The macOS keychain command receives the plaintext profile in its process argument list.
remediation.suggestion: Use a keychain API or stdin-based helper that never places candidate profile data in command-line arguments.

remediation.issue: Relay endpoints can be redirected through environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Display the effective endpoint, require HTTPS, and restrict production transmissions to an allowlisted origin unless the user explicitly approves another destination.

content.value_statement: Job searches require repeated assessment, form completion, and accurate tracking. This skill organizes authorized applications with verified candidate data and submission safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Stores a validated candidate profile using macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager.
Imports a local PDF or read-only Google Docs resume into private local storage.
Scores roles against eligibility, seniority, compensation, location, work mode, and documented requirements.
Checks duplicate applications and enforces cooldown rules before ledger entries are added.
Tracks submissions, outcomes, attention items, workflow rounds, and review metrics in local ledgers.
Supports controlled browser-assisted filling and submission for candidate-authorized applications.
limitations: Secure profile storage is unavailable on Linux.
Browser automation requires a compatible browser tool and an existing authenticated session.
The workflow stops for MFA, CAPTCHA, legal attestations, sensitive identifiers, and uncertain candidate answers.
Telemetry and community job sharing are enabled by default unless the user disables them.

use_cases.title: Organize a Personal Job Search
use_cases.description: Create a verified profile, import a resume, and track each authorized application from discovery through outcome.

use_cases.title: Assess Technical Roles
use_cases.description: Compare postings with documented skills, eligibility, seniority, location, and compensation requirements before applying.

use_cases.title: Manage Authorized Application Batches
use_cases.description: Process an approved set of roles while enforcing duplicate checks, submission gates, and attention queues.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up My Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create my job-search profile from this local resume: [path]. Ask only for required facts that the resume does not provide.

prompt_templates.title: Assess One Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this job posting: [URL]. Check eligibility and must-have evidence, then explain whether I should review, skip, ask, or exclude it.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Authorized Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare my application for [URL]. Use only verified profile facts, stop at protected questions, and request approval before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Review a Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Process these authorized job URLs: [URLs]. Enforce all eligibility and duplicate gates, queue blockers, record confirmed submissions, and summarize outcome metrics.

output_examples.input: Assess a senior backend role with remote work and an unclear sponsorship policy.
output_examples.output: Decision: Ask. The role and work mode match, but work authorization remains unclear. Submission is paused until sponsorship is confirmed.

output_examples.input: Check whether a previously seen role can be submitted.
output_examples.output: Submission blocked. The canonical job URL matches an existing ledger entry, so the application is treated as a hard duplicate.
The review summarizes unique submissions, mature outcomes, interview quality, rejection reasons, source performance, and proposed targeting changes for candidate approval.

best_practices: Use a verified resume and provide candidate facts directly when required information is missing.
Review eligibility, required evidence, compensation, and the final form before every submission.
Disable telemetry and community sharing before use when external data transmission is not acceptable.
anti_patterns: Do not invent experience, authorization, compensation, or answers that the candidate did not provide.
Do not bypass duplicate gates, MFA, CAPTCHA, legal attestations, or browser confirmation requirements.
Do not grant routine autonomy without a clear destination, scope, and submission authorization.

faq.question: Can this skill submit applications automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, but only within an authorized routine workflow that passes every eligibility, evidence, score, and duplicate gate.

faq.question: Where is candidate data stored?
faq.answer: Profiles use macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager. Resumes and ledgers use an owner-only local state directory.

faq.question: Does it work on Linux?
faq.answer: Most scripts can run, but secure profile storage intentionally rejects Linux.

faq.question: Does it answer protected or sensitive questions?
faq.answer: No. It stops for demographic questions, government identifiers, legal attestations, MFA, CAPTCHA, and unsupported candidate judgments.

faq.question: Does it send data over the network?
faq.answer: Yes. Analytics and community job sharing use a remote relay by default, and Google Docs resume imports contact Google.

faq.question: Can I disable external analytics and sharing?
faq.answer: Yes. Telemetry and community source sharing have separate disable and reset controls.
